title: The association between changes in health behaviors and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults: A national cross-sectional study
abstract: Background: Depressive symptoms are common in older adults. However, few studies have assessed changes in health behaviors during the pandemic and gender differences among Chinese older adults. Objective: To examine the association of changes in health behaviors with depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults during the pandemic, and gender differences. Methods: The data were obtained from the 2020 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, which included 7,947 older adults. Binary logistic regression examined associations between changes in health behaviors and depressive symptoms, and subgroup analyses assessed gender differences in effects of physical activity, smoking, and alcohol consumption changes on depressive symptoms. Results: The prevalence of depressive symptoms among older adults in China was 39.37% during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Female (odds ratio [OR] = 1.790, 95% CI: 1.578–2.031), unmarried (OR = 1.438, 95% CI: 1.266–1.634), rural residency (OR = 1.479, 95% CI: 1.321–1.657), and two or more chronic diseases (OR = 1.472, 95% CI: 1.253–1.729) were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. Decreased intense activities (OR=1.301, 95% CI: 1.133–1.493) and decreased smoking (OR = 1.500, 95% CI: 1.183–1.903) were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. Subgroup analyses revealed a significant interaction between gender and changes in alcohol consumption on depressive symptoms. Conclusion: The study found that decreased intense activities and decreased smoking were associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms. Health administrators should develop policies based on the relationship between changes in health behaviors and depressive symptoms among older adults of different genders.
